📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iraq’s Minister of Communications announces the issuance of a commemorative stamp marking the grand funeral ceremony of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, in the holy city of Najaf Ashraf.

Mustafa Sand said that a ceremonial stamp has been issued on the occasion of the majestic funeral ceremony for the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution in the cities of Najaf and Karbala.
​
The memorial postage issue has been released to honor the grand funeral ceremony that Iraq is witnessing in tribute to the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, serving as a symbol of recording this event in the country’s historical memory, he said.
​
The funeral procession for the martyred Leader began early on Wednesday in Najaf with the massive presence of Iraqi citizens, pilgrims, and political and religious figures, and was held under special security and service arrangements.
​
Earlier, late on Tuesday, the sacred bodies of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution and several members of his family were formally received at Najaf International Airport by senior officials of the Islamic Republic of Iran and Iraq.

🔻 Navy commander: Iranian shores will become hell for any invading force

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Chief of the Iranian Army for Coordination Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari says any attempt by foreign forces to land on Iran’s shores would be met with overwhelming resistance, warning that the country’s coastline would become “a hell”  for any invading force.

Speaking in a televised interview on Wednesday, Sayyari described any attempt to land foreign troops on Iranian territory as a red line for the Iranian nation, adding that the United States had planned such an operation but failed to carry it out.
​
He said the Iranian Army, together with the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), law enforcement forces, the Basij, and the Iranian people, stand fully prepared to defend the country, adding that no amount of rhetoric would give Washington the courage to undertake such an operation.
​
“The enemy knows that if it commits such a folly and lands forces on Iran’s coast, it will enter a hell from which there will be no escape,” the commander said.
​
He dismissed US President Donald Trump’s claims that Iran’s naval forces had been destroyed, saying the remarks were intended to suggest that Washington could deploy troops along the Makran coast or near the Strait of Hormuz.
​
Washington’s statements were aimed at portraying Iran’s coastline as vulnerable to military intervention, he said, adding that the United States is waging psychological warfare through repeated public statements intended to intimidate the Iranian people.
​
Sayyari assured the public that Iran’s Armed Forces remain fully prepared to defend the country, saying the nation’s borders are secure and that no threat to Iran’s territorial integrity would be tolerated.
